**Subject: Order TH-48217 not received – replacement or full refund required by 13 November**

Hello Tiny Hands Edu Supplies Customer Service,

I am writing again about order **TH-48217**, which has been marked as delivered but has never arrived at my school. I have now emailed twice and spent 38 minutes on hold by phone, and I am no closer to receiving either the supplies or my money back.

I placed the order on **21 October** and paid **R1,640 by card**, including the **R95 delivery fee**. The order was for six tubs of finger paint, four bags of playdough, 200 paper plates, googly eyes, glitter glue and two rolls of brown paper. It was addressed correctly to **Bergview Pre-Primary in Plumstead**.

According to your tracking, the parcel was delivered on **Tuesday, 3 November at 11:42**, and signed for by **“M. Adams”**. There is nobody at the school with that name. Our gate guard, Uncle Faizel, keeps a written record of every delivery, and there is no entry for this parcel on 3 November. The supplies have not been received by the school, and a tracking update with an unfamiliar signature does not change that.

I emailed you on **4 November and again on 6 November**. Both times, I received essentially the same reply: “we have escalated your query to our courier partner”. When I phoned on Friday, after waiting 38 minutes, I was told that nothing could be done until the courier had completed its investigation, which could take another ten working days.

I understand that deliveries can go wrong. What I do not accept is being expected to carry the cost and inconvenience while your courier investigates. My contract is with **Tiny Hands Edu Supplies**, not the courier. I paid you directly, I did not choose the courier, and it should not be my responsibility to sort out your delivery arrangement. You are welcome to investigate with the courier, but that needs to happen separately from resolving this order with me.

These are not personal luxuries. I bought classroom supplies with my own money, on a teacher’s salary, and I am currently **R1,640 out of pocket**. The children have already made the patterns for their masks, and I have been telling them for a week that the paint is “coming soon”. We also need these materials for props for our end-of-year concert on **27 November**, so waiting indefinitely is simply not workable.

I am asking you to resolve this in one of two ways **by Friday, 13 November**:

1. **Resend the complete order at no additional cost**, with confirmation of dispatch and a delivery date that leaves enough time before the concert. If you cannot guarantee this, please do not offer a replacement that will arrive too late; or  
2. **Refund the full R1,640, including the R95 delivery fee**, to the card I used to pay.

Please also have someone respond to the specific information in this email rather than sending another template or telling me that my query has been escalated. I need a clear answer confirming which resolution you are providing.

I have ordered from Tiny Hands Edu Supplies three times before without any problems, which is partly why this experience has been so disappointing. I would prefer to resolve this directly with you. However, if I have not received a proper response and confirmation of either the replacement or the full refund by 13 November, I will dispute the card payment with my bank and leave an honest review describing my experience.

Please treat this as urgent and come back to me with an actual resolution.

Regards,  
[Your full name]  
Bergview Pre-Primary  
[Contact number]
